longTitle.officialTitle: To establish the United States Semiquincentennial Commission, and for other purposes.

main.enactingFormula: Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled,

section.heading: SHORT TITLE.
section.content: This Act may be cited as the “United States Semiquincentennial Commission Act of 2016”.

subsection.heading: Findings.—
subsection.chapeau: Congress finds that July 4, 2026, the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States, as marked by the Declaration of Independence in 1776, and the historic events preceding that anniversary—

paragraph.content: are of major significance in the development of the national heritage of the United States of individual liberty, representative government, and the attainment of equal and inalienable rights; and
have had a profound influence throughout the world.

subsection.heading: Purpose.—
subsection.content: The purpose of this Act is to establish a Commission to provide for the observance and commemoration of the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States and related events through local, State, national, and international activities planned, encouraged, developed, and coordinated by a national commission representative of appropriate public and private authorities and organizations.

paragraph.heading: Commission.—
paragraph.content: The term “Commission” means the United States Semiquincentennial Commission established by section 4(a).

paragraph.heading: Private citizen.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “private citizen” means an individual who is not an officer or employee of—

subparagraph.content: the Federal Government; or
a State or local government.

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of the Interior.

subsection.heading: In general.—
subsection.content: There is established a commission, to be known as the “United States Semiquincentennial Commission”, to plan, encourage, develop, and coordinate the commemoration of the history of the United States leading up to the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States.

subsection.heading: Composition.—
subsection.chapeau: The Commission shall be composed of the following members:

paragraph.chapeau: Four members of the Senate, of whom—

subparagraph.content: two shall be appointed by the majority leader of the Senate; and
two shall be appointed by the minority leader of the Senate.

paragraph.chapeau: Four members of the House of Representatives, of whom—

subparagraph.content: two shall be appointed by the Speaker of the House of Representatives; and
two shall be appointed by the minority leader of the House of Representatives.

paragraph.chapeau: Sixteen members who are private citizens, of whom—

subparagraph.content: four shall be appointed by the majority leader of the Senate;
four shall be appointed by the minority leader of the Senate;
four shall be appointed by the Speaker of the House of Representatives;
four shall be appointed by the minority leader of the House of Representatives; and
one of whom shall be designated by the President as the Chairperson.

paragraph.chapeau: The following nonvoting ex officio members:

subparagraph.content: The Secretary.
The Secretary of State.
The Attorney General.
The Secretary of Defense.
The Secretary of Education.
The Librarian of Congress.
The Secretary of the Smithsonian Institution.
The Archivist of the United States.
The Chairperson of the National Endowment for the Arts.
The Chairperson of the National Endowment for the Humanities.
The Director of the Institute of Museum and Library Services.

clause.content: The Chief Justice of the United States; or
an Associate Justice or former Associate Justice appointed by the Chief Justice of the United States.

paragraph.heading: Term.—
paragraph.content: A member shall be appointed for the life of the Commission.

subparagraph.content: shall not affect the powers of the Commission; and
shall be filled in the same manner as the original appointment was made.

paragraph.heading: Removal of members who are private citizens.—
paragraph.content: Following notice and approval of the relevant appointing authority, on an affirmative vote of not less than ⅔ of the members of the Commission, the Commission may remove a member of the Commission appointed under subsection (b)(3).

paragraph.heading: Location of first meeting.—
paragraph.content: The first meeting of the Commission shall be convened at Independence Hall in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, to honor the historical significance of the building as the site of deliberations and adoption of both the United States Declaration of Independence and Constitution.

paragraph.heading: Location of subsequent meetings.—
paragraph.content: At least 1 meeting of the Commission each year shall be held in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

subsection.heading: Quorum.—
subsection.content: A majority of the members of the Commission shall constitute a quorum, but a lesser number of members may hold hearings.

paragraph.content: prepare an overall program for commemorating the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States and the historic events preceding that anniversary; and
plan, encourage, develop, and coordinate observances and activities commemorating the historic events that preceded, and are associated with, the United States Semiquincentennial.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: In preparing plans and an overall program, the Commission—

subparagraph.content: shall give due consideration to any related plans and programs developed by State, local, and private groups; and
may designate special committees with representatives from groups described in subparagraph (A) to plan, develop, and coordinate specific activities.

subparagraph.chapeau: emphasize the planning of events in locations of historical significance to the United States, especially in those locations that witnessed the assertion of American liberty, such as—

clause.content: leading cities, including Boston, Charleston, New York City, and Philadelphia; and
the role of persons and locations with significant impact on the history of the United States during the 250-year period beginning on the date of execution of the Declaration of Independence; and
the ideas associated with that history, which have been so important in the development of the United States, in world affairs, and in the quest for freedom of all mankind.

subparagraph.content: evaluate existing infrastructure;

include in the report required under subsection (c) recommendations for what infrastructure should be in place for the successful undertaking of an appropriate celebration in accordance with this Act; and
coordinate with State and local bodies to make necessary infrastructure improvements.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Not later than March 31, 2020, the Commission shall submit to the President a comprehensive report that includes the specific recommendations of the Commission for the commemoration of the 250th anniversary and related events.

paragraph.heading: Recommended activities.—
paragraph.chapeau: The report may include recommended activities such as—

subparagraph.content: the production, publication, and distribution of books, pamphlets, films, and other educational materials focusing on the history, culture, and political thought of the period of the American Revolution;
bibliographical and documentary projects and publications;

conferences, convocations, lectures, seminars, and other programs, especially those located in the 13 colonies, including the major cities and buildings of national historical significance of the 13 colonies;
the development of libraries, museums, historic sites, and exhibits, including mobile exhibits;

subparagraph.chapeau: ceremonies and celebrations commemorating specific events, such as—

clause.content: the signing of the Declaration of Independence;
programs and activities focusing on the national and international significance of the United States Semiquincentennial; and
the implications of the Semiquincentennial for present and future generations; and

subparagraph.content: encouraging Federal agencies to integrate the celebration of the Semiquincentennial into the regular activities and execution of the purpose of the agencies through such activities as the issuance of coins, medals, certificates of recognition, stamps, and the naming of vessels.

the recommendations of the Commission for the allocation of financial and administrative responsibility among the public and private authorities and organizations recommended for participation by the Commission; and
proposals for such legislative enactments and administrative actions as the Commission considers necessary to carry out the recommendations.

subsection.heading: Report Submitted to Congress.—
subsection.chapeau: The President shall submit to Congress a report that contains—

paragraph.content: the complete report of the Commission; and
such comments and recommendations for legislation and such a description of administrative actions taken by the President as the President considers appropriate.

subsection.heading: Point of Contact.—
subsection.content: The Commission, acting through the secretariat of the Commission described in section 9(b), shall serve as the point of contact of the Federal Government for all State, local, international, and private sector initiatives regarding the Semiquincentennial of the founding of the United States, with the purpose of coordinating and facilitating all fitting and proper activities honoring the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States.

subsection.heading: In general.—
subsection.content: In carrying out this Act, the Commission shall consult and cooperate with, and seek advice and assistance from, appropriate Federal agencies, State and local public bodies, learned societies, and historical, patriotic, philanthropic, civic, professional, and related organizations.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Federal agencies shall cooperate with the Commission in planning, encouraging, developing, and coordinating appropriate commemorative activities.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall undertake a study of appropriate actions that might be taken to further preserve and develop historic sites and battlefields, at such time and in such manner as will ensure that fitting observances and exhibits may be held at appropriate sites and battlefields during the 250th anniversary celebration.

subparagraph.heading: Report.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall submit to the Commission a report that contains the results of the study and the recommendations of the Secretary, in time to afford the Commission an opportunity—

clause.content: to incorporate in the report described in section 5(c) such findings and recommendations as the Commission considers appropriate.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Chairperson of the National Endowment for the Arts, the Chairperson of the National Endowment for the Humanities, and the Director of the Institute of Museum and Library Services shall cooperate with the Commission, especially in the encouragement and coordination of scholarly works and artistic expressions focusing on the history, culture, and political thought of the period predating the United States Semiquincentennial.

subparagraph.heading: Library of congress, smithsonian institution, and archives.—

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: The Librarian of Congress, the Secretary of the Smithsonian Institution, and the Archivist of the United States shall cooperate with the Commission, especially in the development and display of exhibits and collections and in the development of bibliographies, catalogs, and other materials relevant to the period predating the United States Semiquincentennial.

clause.heading: Location.—
clause.content: To the maximum extent practicable, displays described in subparagraph (A) shall be located in, or in facilities near to, buildings of historical significance to the American Revolution, so as to promote greater public awareness of the heritage of the United States.

subparagraph.heading: Submission of recommendations.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Each of the officers described in this paragraph shall submit to the Commission a report containing recommendations in time to afford the Commission an opportunity—

clause.content: to incorporate in the report described in section 5(c) such findings and recommendations as the Commission considers appropriate.

paragraph.heading: Department of state.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary of State shall coordinate the participation of foreign nations in the celebration of the United States Semiquincentennial, including by soliciting the erection of monuments and other cultural cooperations in founding and other cities of the United States so as—

subparagraph.content: to celebrate the shared heritage of the United States with the many peoples and nations of the world; and
to provide liaison and encouragement for the erection of international pavilions to showcase the spread of democratic institutions abroad in the period following the American Revolution.

subsection.heading: Hearings.—
subsection.content: The Commission may hold such hearings, meet and act at such times and places, take such testimony, and receive such evidence as the Commission considers advisable to carry out this Act.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Commission may secure directly from a Federal agency such information as the Commission considers necessary to carry out this Act.

paragraph.heading: Provision of information.—
paragraph.content: On request of the Chairperson of the Commission, the head of the agency shall provide the information to the Commission.

subsection.heading: Postal Services.—
subsection.content: The Commission may use the United States mails in the same manner and under the same conditions as other agencies of the Federal Government.

subsection.heading: Gifts.—
subsection.content: The Commission may accept, use, and dispose of gifts or donations of money, property, or personal services.

subsection.heading: Additional Powers.—
subsection.chapeau: As determined necessary by the Commission, the Commission may—

paragraph.content: procure supplies, services, and property;
make contracts;
expend in furtherance of this Act funds donated or received in pursuance of contracts entered into under this Act; and
take such actions as are necessary to enable the Commission to carry out efficiently and in the public interest the purposes of this Act.

paragraph.heading: Time capsule.—
paragraph.chapeau: A representative portion of all books, manuscripts, miscellaneous printed matter, memorabilia, relics, and other materials relating to the United States Semiquincentennial shall be deposited in a time capsule—

subparagraph.content: to be buried in Independence Mall, Philadelphia, on July 4, 2026; and
to be unearthed on the occasion of the 500th anniversary of the United States of America on July 4, 2276.

paragraph.heading: Other materials.—
paragraph.content: All other books, manuscripts, miscellaneous printed matter, memorabilia, relics, and other materials relating to the United States Semiquincentennial, whether donated to the Commission or collected by the Commission, may be deposited for preservation in national, State, or local libraries or museums or be otherwise disposed of by the Commission, in consultation with the Librarian of Congress, the Secretary of the Smithsonian Institution, the Archivist of the United States, and the Administrator of General Services.

subsection.heading: Property.—
subsection.chapeau: Any property acquired by the Commission remaining on termination of the Commission may be—

paragraph.content: used by the Secretary for purposes of the National Park Service; or
disposed of as excess or surplus property.

subsection.heading: Compensation of Members.—
subsection.content: The members of the Commission shall receive no compensation for service on the Commission.

subsection.heading: Travel Expenses.—
subsection.content: A member of the Commission shall be allowed travel expenses, including per diem in lieu of subsistence, at rates authorized for an employee of an agency under subchapter I of chapter 57 of title 5, United States Code, while away from the home or regular place of business of the member in the performance of the duties of the Commission.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Chairperson of the Commission may, without regard to the civil service laws (including regulations), appoint and terminate an executive director and such other additional personnel as are necessary to enable the Commission to perform the duties of the Commission.

paragraph.heading: Confirmation of executive director.—
paragraph.content: The employment of an executive director shall be subject to confirmation by the Commission.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Except as provided in subparagraph (B), the Chairperson of the Commission may fix the compensation of the executive director and other personnel without regard to the provisions of chapter 51 and subchapter III of chapter 53 of title 5, United States Code, relating to classification of positions and General Schedule pay rates.

subparagraph.heading: Maximum rate of pay.—
subparagraph.content: The rate of pay for the executive director and other personnel shall not exceed the rate payable for level V of the Executive Schedule under section 5316 of title 5, United States Code.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: An employee of the Federal Government may be detailed to the Commission without reimbursement.

paragraph.heading: Civil service status.—
paragraph.content: The detail of the employee shall be without interruption or loss of civil service status or privilege.

subsection.heading: Procurement of Temporary and Intermittent Services.—
subsection.content: The Chairperson of the Commission may procure temporary and intermittent services in accordance with section 3109(b) of title 5, United States Code, at rates for individuals that do not exceed the daily equivalent of the annual rate of basic pay prescribed for level V of the Executive Schedule under section 5316 of that title.

subsection.heading: Advisory Committees.—
subsection.content: The Commission may appoint such advisory committees as the Commission determines necessary.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: All expenditures of the Commission shall be made from donations, earned income, and any funds made available to carry out this Act under subsection (f).

subsection.heading: Administrative Secretariat.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary of the Interior shall, through a competitive process, seek to enter into an arrangement with a nonprofit organization, the mission of which is consistent with the purpose of this Act. Under such arrangement, such nonprofit organization shall—

paragraph.content: serve as the secretariat of the Commission, including by serving as the point of contact under section 5(e);
house the administrative offices of the Commission;
assume responsibility for funds of the Commission; and
provide to the Commission financial and administrative services, including services related to budgeting, accounting, financial reporting, personnel, and procurement.

subsection.heading: Payment for Financial and Administrative Services.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Subject to paragraph (2), payment for services provided under subsection (b)(4) shall be made in advance, or by reimbursement, from funds of the Commission in such amounts as may be agreed on by the Chairperson of the Commission and the secretariat of the Commission.

subparagraph.heading: Erroneous payments.—
subparagraph.content: The regulations under section 5514 of title 5, United States Code, relating to the collection of indebtedness of personnel resulting from erroneous payments shall apply to the collection of erroneous payments made to, or on behalf of, a Commission employee.

subparagraph.heading: No promulgation by commission.—
subparagraph.content: The Commission shall not be required to prescribe any regulations relating to the matters described in subparagraph (A).

subsection.heading: Annual Report.—
subsection.content: Annually during the period beginning 1 year after the Commission submits the report to the President under section 5(c)(1) and ending on December 31, 2027, the Commission shall submit to Congress a report of the activities of the Commission, including an accounting of funds received and expended during the year covered by the report.

subsection.heading: Intellectual Property Protections.—
subsection.content: The Commission shall have the exclusive right to use, and to allow others to use, the official marks, imprimaturs, and logos of the Commission.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There are authorized to be appropriated such sums as are necessary to carry out this Act.

section.heading: TERMINATION OF COMMISSION.
section.content: The Commission shall terminate on December 31, 2027.
